author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
description:
Survey reveals medics were called ‘monkeys’ and ‘dirty foreigners’, and patients refused to be seen by black or Asian staff

NHS radiographers are experiencing racist abuse by patients, who have called them “monkeys” and refused to be seen by black and Asian staff, according to a report.

A survey of 381 members of the Society of Radiographers revealed a “noticeable” rise in instances of overt racism experienced and witnessed by radiographers across the health service over the past 18 months.

Continue reading...
title: NHS radiographers report rise in overt racist abuse by patients

author: Maya Yang
description:
Trump ‘disappointed’ with US attorney amid reports he’s considering removing her from her post

  • Trump’s reflecting pool saga: a timeline

Donald Trump accused US attorney Jeanine Pirro of having “folded like an umbrella” amid reports that he was considering removing her from her post.

Trump criticized Pirro on Monday after she dropped vandalism charges against a former Olympian accused of damaging the recently renovated Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool. Trump nominated Pirro to serve as interim US attorney for the District of Columbia last year, and the Senate
title: Trump accuses Jeanine Pirro of ‘folding’ by dropping reflecting pool charges

author: Rajeev Syal and Alexandra Topping
description:
Andy Burnham will also delay release of thousands of prisoners across England and Wales a month, until October

Rapists, child sexual abusers and groomers will be excluded from early release plans to ease critical prison overcrowding in a major intervention by Andy Burnham.

The prime minister said on Tuesday that he will delay the planned early release of thousands of prisoners across England and Wales by a month until October.

Continue reading...
title: Rapists, child abusers and groomers will not leave prison early, says PM

author: Martin Farrer
description:
Two men were arrested on Monday evening and one was charged over an alleged replica pistol. Follow today’s news live.

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

NSW police have arrested and charged two men after one of them allegedly brandished a fake replica gun, wearing a bulletproof vest with a US flag and carrying a toy police badge, at a busy Sydney entertainment precinct, AAP reports.

Uniform and specialist police swarmed the pair at the Entertainment Quarter at Moore Park on Monday afternoon.
title: Australia news live: charges laid after alleged replica gun scare in Sydney entertainment spot

author: Maya Yang
description:
Threats come as questions surround death of Mississippi teenager, who was found dead after boat trip with friends

Several people with no apparent connection to the Nolan Wells case have been criminally charged with making threats amid questions surrounding the Mississippi teenager’s death in July.

The death of the 18-year-old Mississippi college freshman has drawn widespread attention since he was found dead following a boat trip to Horn Island, several miles off the Mississippi Gulf coast, with a group of friends.

Continue reading...
title: Nolan Wells death: at least two people charged over alleged threats to officials

author: Helena Smith in Athens
description:
Inquiries have focused on Elisabeth-Jane Ross’s last few hours alive and police believe they hold the key to why 38-year-old was targeted

Greek authorities are investigating what may have motivated a 26-year-old Afghan man to kill a Scottish charity worker found dead in a suitcase in an abandoned building in Athens last month.

Inquiries have focused increasingly on Elisabeth-Jane Ross’s last few hours alive and police believe they hold the key to revealing why the 38-year-old was targeted.

Continue reading...
title: Greek authorities investigate motive behind murder of Scottish woman found inside suitcase

author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
description:
Joshua Bonehill-Paine, creator of satirical Crewkerne Gazette, has convictions including for harassing a Jewish MP

A former neo-Nazi activist with convictions including for harassing a Jewish MP has been selected as a Conservative candidate for a local election in Somerset.

Joshua Bonehill-Paine, the creator of the viral Crewkerne Gazette series of AI clips, is due to stand for election to Somerset council next year in a new Crewkerne South district. He told the Guardian he was an executive member of the Tories’ Yeovil branch, working as an events organiser.

Continue reading...
title: Former neo-Nazi activist selected as Tory candidate for Somerset council election

author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
description:
Restore leader has countered charges he’s splitting the right while showing his party is a very real obstacle for Reform

Even by the standards of their rivalry, the speed at which Rupert Lowe’s olive branch to Nigel Farage morphed into fresh recriminations between the two was swift.

It began with a softly lit 12-minute video posted on Sunday by the Restore Britain leader, looking straight to camera and referring to “Nigel” as he suggested his party could be willing to cast aside its differences with Reform UK and work together.

Continue reading...
title: Rupert Lowe’s ‘olive branch’ to Farage piles more pressure on Reform leader

author: Andrew Roth
description:
US president reduced to bemoaning Tehran’s ‘unbelievable duplicity’ as he struggles to find solid negotiating ground

  • Middle East crisis live – latest updates

The Donald Trump doctrine has always contained a tenuous relationship with the truth. It was his mentor, the infamous New York lawyer Roy Cohn, who taught the young real estate mogul always to claim victory and never to admit defeat. Unfortunately for Trump, in Iran the US president has found a counterpart just as stubborn as himself.

As Trump claims new negotiations are to begin with Tehran this week, Iran has shown it can also reignite the conflict by lobbing ballistic missiles at US bases in the region and maintaining a stranglehold on
title: Trump meets his obstinate match in Iran’s hardball regime

author: Diane Taylor
description:
Ruling quashes Home Office policy to refuse asylum seekers’ right to have trafficking claims reconsidered after initial rejection

A high court judge has ordered the Home Office to bring an alleged victim of trafficking forcibly removed to France under the “one in one out” scheme back to the UK.

It is the first ruling of its kind and could lead to more people affected by the “one in one out” policy being brought back to the UK.

Continue reading...
title: Judge orders return of alleged victim of trafficking sent to France under ‘one in one out’ scheme

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Author says elements of missing section included questions on Biden’s decision to run for re-election, the Times reports

The author of an infamous internal Democrat party report on the 2024 presidential election loss has claimed that an entire section that included a discussion of generational wealth established by high-ranking elected officials was cut from the draft version leaked and later released earlier this summer.

Paul Rivera, the author of the autopsy, told the New York Times that a section titled “What Happened in 2024” was missing from the published version but had been included in the version he personally handed to embattled party chairman Ken Martin in January.

Continue reading...
title: Author of Democrats’ 2024 election autopsy report says chapter was left out

author: Reuters
description:
US sees first fatalities due to intestinal illness, though both had significant ​underlying health conditions

Two people have died from cyclosporiasis in Michigan, the state’s health department said on Monday, marking the first fatalities in the largest US outbreak ⁠of the intestinal illness.

Both ⁠individuals had significant ​underlying health conditions that may have been affected by cyclosporiasis and dehydration, according to medical records.

Continue reading...
title: US cyclosporiasis outbreak kills two people in Michigan, officials say

author: Robyn Vinter
description:
NatureScot refuses licence for hunt on Hebridean island of Sula Sgeir in which up to 2,000 gannet chicks are killed

A controversial Scottish seabird hunt will not go ahead for the first time in 400 years, in what campaigners have called a “victory for common sense”.

In the annual guga hunt, up to 2,000 gannet chicks are killed over a 10-day period on the uninhabited Hebridean island of Sula Sgeir, 40 miles north of Lewis and Harris.

Continue reading...
title: Scottish seabird hunt cancelled for first time in 400 years

author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
description:
European Commission president says work needed in five areas of migration control including returning more people

The president of the European Commission has called for action to strengthen Europe’s borders after tens of thousands of people arrived and quickly left the Spanish territory of Ceuta, triggering a furious row between Madrid and other European countries.

In a letter to Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, on Monday, Ursula von der Leyen said: “From this incident, it is clear that we must do more to further strengthen our borders at critical points, including vigilant monitoring and the use of physical barriers where needed.”

Continue reading...
title: Stronger EU borders needed after Ceuta crisis, von der Leyen says

author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
description:
Nathan Owen drove his electric Jaguar at up to 86mph and lied to police it was malfunctioning and out of his control

A man who drove his electric Jaguar at up to 86mph on motorways falsely telling police the car was malfunctioning and out of his control has been jailed for four years and three months.

Nathan Owen fabricated not being able to brake in a “frighteningly stupid” ploy to avoid paying car finance, Liverpool crown court heard.

Continue reading...
title: Driver jailed for four years after faking brake failure on motorway

author: Richard Luscombe and agencies
description:
Representative who did not seek re-election in 2024 died of Alzheimer’s disease, her son said

Kay Granger, who served in the US House for almost three decades as the first elected Republican woman from Texas, died on Sunday, her family said. She was 83.

The cause of death, according to her son JD Granger, was Alzheimer’s disease.

Continue reading...
title: Kay Granger, first Texas Republican woman elected to House, dies aged 83

author: Presented by Lucy Houghwith Ashifa Kassam; produced by Annie La Vespaand Bryony Moore; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin
description:
Dozens of people died attempting to reach the Spanish enclave of Ceuta after an estimated 50,000 crossed from Morocco last week. The incident has led to a political crisis in Spain and criticism from EU countries.

Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s European community affairs correspondent, Ashifa Kassam – watch on YouTube

Continue reading...
title: How Ceuta migrant crisis exposes divisions within Europe - The Latest

author: Press Association
description:
Family update on GoFundMe page says child, who was six when badly injured in 2019 incident, is now back at school

A boy thrown from the viewing balcony in the Tate Modern art gallery has a “smile back on his face” after being discharged from hospital, his family have said.

The French youngster, who name remains undisclosed for privacy reasons, was six when he was badly hurt in an attack by then teenager Jonty Bravery at the London attraction on August 4 2019.

Continue reading...
title: French boy thrown from Tate balcony has ‘smile back’ after hospital release

author: Shrai Popat and Guardian staff in Washington
description:
Move comes after Blanche gives senators written assurance he will drop Trump’s $1.8bn anti-weaponization fund

Two Republican senators who threatened to block Todd Blanche’s bid to permanently become attorney general announced they will advance his nomination after he confirmed in writing that a planned $1.8bn slush fund for Donald Trump’s allies was dead.

The US Senate judiciary committee is due to vote on Tuesday on whether to approve the nomination of Blanche, who is already acting attorney general, and send it to the wider Senate for a vote.

Continue reading...
title: Republican holdouts say they will back Todd Blanche for attorney general

author: Presented by Jessica Elgot and Alexandra Topping, produced by Frankie Tobi and Nada Smiljanic, music by Axel Kacoutié; the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj.
description:
Nigel Farage has promised that Reform UK would call in the navy to tackle small boat Channel crossings. Will this familiar-sounding immigration policy distract from the party’s internal problems? Plus – as we learn more about Andy Burnham’s plans for devolution, is this the biggest rewiring of the UK state since the second world war?

Read about Richard Tice being investigated by parliament’s standards watchdog here

You can read Alexandra’s report on Andy Burnham’s trip to Dover here and about constitutional reform here

Please keep sending your comments and questions to pol
title: What chaos? Farage tries to distract with immigration plans – podcast

author: Guardian staff
description:
The host tore into ‘wildly invasive’ cameras, microphones and license plate readers that police use to track Americans

John Oliver discussed the tools that police are using to keep track of Americans on the latest episode of Last Week Tonight.

In recent years, the use of surveillance technology has exploded among local police forces due to decreasing prices and federal funding, with one local mayor comparing modern systems to “Big Brother on steroids”.

Continue reading...
title: John Oliver on police surveillance: ‘Big Brother on steroids’

author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
description:
Expert says people face being filmed without their consent as $89 Anko smartglasses sell out in stores and online

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Kmart has sold out of Anko-branded $89 camera glasses across Australia, which a digital rights expert says presents a “privacy nightmare” as people face being filmed without their consent.

As of Monday, the clear-lens, black-rimmed glasses, which can capture images and record high-definition videos, were sold out at Kmart stores across Australia and online.

Continue reading...
title: Kmart sells out of low-cost rival to Meta camera glasses across Australia amid warnings of ‘privacy nightmare’

author: Ben Doherty
description:
His legal strategy was apparent from the very first. Jones will, it was explicitly stated, seek to undermine the ‘credibility and reliability’ of his accusers

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Alan Jones has enjoyed decades as the centre of attention, as the wielder of power.

The booming voice, the vast radio audience, the bully pulpit of an eponymous TV show, the great and the good on speed-dial, a staffer in the prime ministerial office dubbed the “minister for Alan Jones”: these were not ancillaries peripheral to the Jones empire, they were central to it.

Continue reading...
title: Alan Jones argues ‘rivalry’ and ‘treachery’ but after decades wielding the sword of public opinion, he’s the one on trial

author: Luca Ittimani
description:
Handful of tollroads to get one-off price cuts but WestConnex toll to keep rising at least 4% a year

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The cost of using Sydney’s biggest toll road will continue to rise at least 4% a year after the multinational private operator was accused of blocking the state government’s push for sweeping reforms.

Only a handful of Sydney’s motorways will receive one-off toll cuts under a deal announced by the state Labor government on Monday, as the tolling bill footed by taxpayers surpasses $1bn.

Continue reading...
title: Most Sydney road tolls to keep rising after Transurban accused of blocking reforms

author: Lorenzo Tondo and agencies
description:
Hungary and Romania face energy crisis as record-low river levels force atomic power plants to reduce output

  • Europe live – latest updates

Romanian naval forces carried out a controlled explosion to help redirect vital cooling water from the drought-hit Danube to the country’s last working nuclear ⁠reactor, as neighbouring Hungary ​said it may be able to eke out two more days of power from its only atomic plant.

Hungary and Romania have been forced to shut down nuclear reactors cooled by the Danube for the first time, as record-low water levels deepen fears of an energy crisis across the region. Romania has declared a nationwide state of emergency throughout August stemming from a decline in electri
title: Romania blasts rock to divert water from drought-hit Danube to nuclear reactor

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Police credited Jordan Salinas with limiting number of victims in attack on restaurant in Twin Falls, Idaho

A healthcare worker returning fire on a 24-year-old gunman who killed three people and wounded several others an In-N-Out Burger in Twin Falls, Idaho, has said his impulse to confront the attacker was “automatic” and “mechanical”.

That description from 35-year-old Jordan Salinas came in an interview with the Idaho Statesman that was published on Sunday, providing a detailed account of actions that police credited with limiting the number of victims in the attack a day earlier.

Continue reading...
title: Man who returned fire at In-N-Out gunman had done firearm training after 2021 mass shooting

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
State supreme court rules in case of two bishops who were silent about three children abused by Mormon parents

Clergy members in Arizona who learn of child abuse in the context of religious confession are not required to report it, the state’s supreme court has said in a ruling that protects what church leaders call the “seal of the confessional”.

The panel’s ruling ends a long-running case in which three children who were sexually abused by their parents sued the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS), also known as the Mormon church, and two bishops who became aware of the crimes but remained silent.

In the US, call or text the Childhelp abuse hotline on 800-422-4453 or visit their website for more resources and to report child abuse or D
title: Arizona clergy who learn of child abuse in confessions aren’t required to report it, court rules

author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
description:
Admission may undermine Farage’s account of circumstances surrounding £5m gift from crypto billionaire

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Nigel Farage has admitted he held talks about the possibility of returning as Reform UK’s leader months before the 2024 general election, potentially undermining his own account of the circumstances in which he received a £5m gift from a crypto billionaire.

It was reported at the weekend Farage had struck a deal with the party’s then leader, Richard Tice, and the convicted fraudster George Cottrell to return to frontline politics.
title: Farage admits he discussed returning as Reform leader months earlier than previously stated

author: Steven Morris
description:
Christopher Phillips, who had been his mother Sylvia’s primary carer since 2008, given two years and four months in prison

A man has been jailed for keeping his dead mother’s body in a freezer at their shared home for almost three years, during which time he received more than £70,000 of her benefits and other funds.

Christopher Phillips, 60, stored the body of Sylvia Phillips, a retired company secretary, in the chest freezer in the living room of their house in the south Wales seaside town of Porthcawl.

Continue reading...
title: Man jailed for keeping dead mother’s body in freezer and pocketing her benefits

author: Michael Savage Media editor
description:
Staff at 5 Live told he will not return following claims about his previous career at Sullivan’s Sport newspapers

The BBC radio presenter Tony Livesey has left the broadcaster after allegations were raised about his previous career as the editor-in-chief of David Sullivan’s Sport newspapers.

Staff at 5 Live, where Livesey had most recently presented the 10pm to 1am show four days a week, were told he would not be returning to the station, having stepped away from the role after the allegations first emerged.

Continue reading...
title: Radio presenter Tony Livesey leaves BBC after David Sullivan allegations

author: Martin Belam
description:
US president says he called off another US attack on Iran as part of a push for an agreement. Plus why Pokémon Go is still bring global joy 10 years on

Good morning. Donald Trump said talks with Iran would happen on Monday but declined to set a deadline for an agreement, after earlier saying he had called ⁠off an imminent attack. For its part, Iran said it was nearing a deal with Oman over a new route through the strait of Hormuz, and it had no plans to receive a delegation or send an Iranian one to any talks.

On Saturday night, Trump claimed on social media that Iran and other Middle Eastern countries had asked for time to complete a deal ⁠that would lead to “the immediate, complete and total” reopening of the strait and “an end to Iran’s nuclear threat”. He added that Tehran must “rapidly make a deal”.

What has Iran said about
title: Trump promises new Iran talks as Tehran touts Hormuz shipping deal with Oman | First Thing

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
Todd Blanche issues formal order to withdraw ‘anti-weaponization fund’ after weeks of negotiations with Republican senators who were blocking his nomination

  • Blanche formally rescinds Trump’s $1.8bn ‘anti-weaponization fund’

  • Sign up for the US Breaking News email

Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US health secretary, on Sunday told American parents that they should get their children vaccinated against
title: Trump’s attorney general pick says he has reached deal with senators after standoff – US politics live

author: Phillip Inman
description:
Factories in upbeat mood despite fears over economic impact of US war on Iran, poll finds

  • Business live – latest updates

UK manufacturers ramped up production last month for the fourth consecutive month and at the fastest pace in almost two years, according to a leading survey of the industry.

The S&P Global poll of manufacturers found them in upbeat mood in July, though anxious about the prospect of a long war in the Middle East that would block supplies of oil and gas, and raise the cost of production.

Continue reading...
title: UK manufacturing growth picks up as Trump tariff chaos eases

author: Reuters
description:
Party’s deputy leader accused of a possible failure to declare an interest, commissioner says ⁠on ​its website

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Britain’s ⁠parliamentary ⁠standards watchdog is ​investigating ⁠Reform UK’s ⁠deputy ​leader, ‌Richard ‌Tice, over ‌a possible failure to declare ‌an interest, ​the commissioner said ⁠on ​its website ​on ​Monday.

More details soon …

Continue reading...
title: Standards watchdog investigating Reform UK’s Richard Tice

author: Associated Press in Wellington
description:
Pacific nation is latest country to signal a shift away from its colonial past with return to its traditional name

The Pacific Island country of Nauru has changed its name to the Republic of Naoero, its president said, matching the spelling and pronunciation in the national language.

The country’s international code will change from NRU to NRO and its people will be known as dei-Naoero instead of Nauruan. Commonly known abroad by the pronunciation of Now-roo, the new name is spoken as Now-ero.

Continue reading...
title: Nauru officially changes its name to Naoero

author: Lisa Cox and Petra Stock
description:
Environment minister says Australia has ‘long and difficult journey’ and says more mass mortality events likely

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Aerial surveillance has detected mass bird deaths in a second Australian state in another suspected escalation of the spread of deadly H5 bird flu.

The environment minister, Murray Watt, said on Monday Australia had begun “a long and difficult journey” as CSIRO analysis confirmed Australia’s first mass mortality event at Baudin Rocks off South Australia
title: Suspected mass bird flu deaths found in second state as Murray Watt warns ‘this is the beginning’

author: Julia Kollewe
description:
Brent crude drops by 5% after US president said talks on Middle East peace deal would resume

  • Business live – latest updates

Crude oil prices fell sharply and European stock markets rallied on Monday after Donald Trump cancelled planned strikes on Iran to focus on negotiations for a peace deal.

Brent crude was trading 5% lower at $83.50 a barrel by mid-morning, after falling as low as $81.55 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate dropped more than $5 to $79.47 a barrel.

Continue reading...
title: Oil prices plunge and Europe’s stock markets rally after Trump calls off Iran strikes

author: Vivian Ho
description:
Iranian spokesperson says there are no plans to receive or send a delegation following US president’s assertion that talks would take place today

  • Trump says Iran talks set for Monday

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Middle East.

Esmaeil Baghaei, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson, told reporters at a weekly press briefing on Monday that Iran is not currently holding any talks with the US, Reuters reports – contradicting claims made by Donald Trump on Sunday night that talks with Iran would happen the next day.

Continue reading...
title: Middle East crisis live: Iran denies Trump’s claims that talks due to take place

author: Kevin Rawlinson
description:
Retired commander says policy lacks substance as party accused of trying to distract from Nigel Farage’s scandals

  • UK politics live – latest updates

A Reform UK proposal to use the military to stop small boats bringing migrants to the UK from France lacks substance, a former Royal Navy officer has said, suggesting the UK’s warships would be better used countering actual military threats.

Reform’s political opponents have claimed its plans have more to do with distracting from the financial scandals surrounding its leader, Nigel Farage, than about solving the small boats issue, after the party proposed having the navy pick up people trying to make irregular Channel crossings and
title: Former navy officer criticises Reform plan to use military to stop small boats

author: Yohannes Lowe
description:
Labour say plan is a ‘desperate attempt to distract from sleaze’ while a retired commander says it ‘lacks substance’

The leader of Restore Britain, Rupert Lowe, told the Reform UK leader, Nigel Farage, that if he was “prepared to work together around serious policies, serious reform and serious government, then so are we”.

In a video posted on X on Sunday, Lowe said:

I truly believe there could be sufficient common ground for our two movements to cooperate collectively, destroy the looming leftwing alliance that will finish off what hope remains for this country.

In my view, failing to even try because of our own personal difficulties is simply not an option. Now is the time to put our differences aside and cooperate for the good of the country that we all love.

Mass deportation of illegal migrants “including women and children”.

Tougher rules on legal migration, a ban on halal and kosher slaughter, the burqa, cousin marriage an
title: Criticism of Reform UK’s pledge to use Navy to stop small boats – politics live

author: Ed Walton for MetDesk
description:
Soaring temperatures continue to sweep parts of Europe, while Okinawa faces powerful winds and storm surges

  • Europe live – latest updates

Unbearable, record-breaking heat has dominated the summer of 2026 across much of Europe. New records were set in central Europe last week, with Wieselburg in Austria registering a new July peak of 40.3C (104.5F). This is particularly significant as it is just 0.2C behind the all-time high, set in the August of 2003.

However, not all of the northern hemisphere has experienced extreme heat and aridity. Vancouver recorded its wettest July since 2016 and the third wettest since 2008, with 33.6mm of rain. While that total may not appear exceptional, it is only a touch above the 1991-2020 climate average, highlighting how unusually dry July has been in the Canadian city over the past dec
title: Weather tracker: Austria breaks heat records as Japan braces for Typhoon Dolphin

author: Julia Kollewe
description:
Tie-up would be one of the biggest-ever pharmaceutical deals and create the world’s fourth-largest drugmaker

  • Business live – latest updates

Britain’s biggest drugmaker AstraZeneca is understood to be in discussions to take over its US rival Bristol Myers Squibb in a deal that would create a near-$400bn (£300bn) pharmaceutical group.

AstraZeneca, run by Pascal Soriot, its longtime chief executive, is the second-biggest listed company in the UK, with a market value of nearly £196bn before the news broke. BMS, headquartered in Princeton and known for its cancer treatments, is worth $133bn.

Continue reading...
title: AstraZeneca holds talks with Bristol Myers Squibb on $400bn merger

author: Amanda Meade
description:
Former 2UE and 2GB radio broadcaster is facing 22 charges. Jones, 85, has pleaded not guilty

  • Alan Jones trial live updates

  • Warning: may contain graphic content

A champion athlete who was 14 when he met Alan Jones has told a Sydney court the broadcaster befriended him after he broke a record, and went on to give him a mobile phone, a car and up to $600 a week.

Complainant J gave evidence on Monday during the first day of Jones’s indecent assault and sexual touching trial at Sydney local court. Jones, 85, has pleaded not guilty.

Continue reading...
title: Alan Jones allegedly gifted cash and car to teenager he kissed after commenting on sprinter’s penis, trial hears

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Local councillor who says he used to work on Daniel Andrews’ security team also part of upper house lineup for November’s state poll

A former Liberal party candidate, the animator behind Pauline Hanson’s anti-woke film and a local councillor who says he worked on former premier Daniel Andrews’ personal protection team have been unveiled as One Nation candidates for the Victorian election.

Pauline Hanson held a press conference on Monday to announce the eight candidates who will lead One Nation’s upper house tickets at the November state election.

Continue reading...
title: One Nation unveils eight Victorian election candidates including former Liberal and anti-woke film animator

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Former rugby league player turned TikTok influencer tells parliamentary inquiry his spiralling addiction to gambling cost him about $1m

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Former rugby league star Luke Bateman has alleged gambling company promoters supplied him with cocaine and alcohol, telling a parliamentary inquiry the betting industry exercised no duty of care.

Bateman, who is now a TikTok star and influential in the
title: Luke Bateman tells inquiry gambling companies supplied him with cocaine and alcohol
